b Use new Racing Brake Fluid RH665 (DOT 4) from Performance Friction Brakes .

b Have a collecting bottle and transparent hose at hand.

Open both brake fluid reservoirs.

Extract the brake fluid.

Pour in new brake fluid.

Apply pressure to the rear right brake caliper.

→ Pour in brake fluid for the rear axle again.

Apply pressure to the rear left brake caliper.

→ Pour in brake fluid for the rear axle again.

Apply pressure to the front right brake caliper.

→ Pour in brake fluid for the front axle again.

Apply pressure to the front left brake caliper.

→ Pour in brake fluid for the front axle again.

Completely bleed the brake system, see Bleeding the brake system on page 375 .

Wet new pistons with brake fluid and insert new seals in brake fluid.

Insert the pistons into the brake caliper bores. Due to the seal, slight resistance is felt when inserting the pistons into the bore. Make sure that the seals are not squeezed or twisted during insertion.

Insert a plastic block in the brake caliper so that the pistons do not fall out.

Apply low pressure to the brake caliper a few times to ensure that the seals are seated correctly.

Attach the brake caliper to the upright.

Attach the brake hose to the brake caliper.

Insert the brake pads.

Top up brake fluid and bleed the brake system, see Bleeding the brake system on page 375 .

lexical.evidence_text:
If brake pads are installed on a different wheel of the car, this can result in large parts of the brake pad breaking off.

When reusing brake pads, make sure that they are installed at the same position as before.

Remove the brake caliper, see Installing/removing of brake disc and brake caliper on page 362 and see Installing/removing of brake disc and brake caliper on page 365 .

Open the brake fluid reservoir.

Extract the brake fluid to prevent overflowing when the brake pistons are pushed back.

Clean the brake pistons with isopropyl or ethanol and push back using a suitable tool.

Insert new brake pads.

NOTICE! Place the brake pad back plate [1] correctly into the pad guides [3] inside the brake caliper [4] .

→ The friction material [2] of the brake pads faces towards the brake disc.

Install the brake caliper, see Installing/removing of brake disc and brake caliper on page 362 and see Installing/removing of brake disc and brake caliper on page 365 .

Top up brake fluid as required.

Apply the brake.

Bleed the brake system, see Bleeding the brake system on page 375 .

After changing the brake pads, check the entire brake system for smooth operation.

Apply low pressure to the brake caliper a few times to ensure that the seals are seated correctly.

Insert the brake pads.

RaceCon is designed for the configuration of control units, data loggers and test interface systems.

RaceCon is an engine calibration interface for customers of the 911 GT3 Cup.

In RaceCon, you can either:

 track the most important engine variables online or

 alter some important parameters to fine- tune the ECU to your purpose

RaceCon can be used to set up the ECU for individual purposes, like:

 specific racetrack

 set up the car / set up for a new or rebuilt engine

RaceCon includes a diagnostic interface to analyze the engine itself and its electronics.

Wet new pistons with brake fluid and insert new seals in brake fluid.

Insert the pistons into the brake caliper bores. Due to the seal, slight resistance is felt when inserting the pistons into the bore. Make sure that the seals are not squeezed or twisted during insertion.

Insert a plastic block in the brake caliper so that the pistons do not fall out.

Apply low pressure to the brake caliper a few times to ensure that the seals are seated correctly.

Attach the brake caliper to the upright.

Attach the brake hose to the brake caliper.

Insert the brake pads.

Top up brake fluid and bleed the brake system, see Bleeding the brake system on page 375 .

Insert the brake pads.

Section: Part B: Specific Technical Regulations, Porsche GT3 Cup, Type 992 (MY 2021-2025) > 22. General information

Technically identical Cars with the designation Porsche 911 GT3 Cup (type 992), built by Porsche AG in a small production run on the basis of the Porsche 911 GT3, shall be used for the Series. Cars of model year 2021-2025 (see following general Car description) are permitted. The Cars must comply with the requirements of these Technical Regulations. Technical acceptance of the Cars is undertaken by the Technical Scrutineers. In addition to the Technical Regulations according to Part A of these Regulations, the following specific Technical Regulations are applicable.
